n827f0d70365.s: The pottery of Kalibangan is classified into how many fabrics?
n827f0d70365.x: Kalibangan's pottery is classified into six fabrics; the settlement also had a mud-brick fortification.

nindian-history-3-34.s: Sutkagendor in Baluchistan, Pakistan, marks which boundary of the Harappan culture?
nindian-history-3-34.x: Sutkagendor marks the western boundary of Harappan culture; Alamgirpur marks the eastern.

n633a8d20ae5.s: Which of the following Harappan sites is NOT correctly matched with the year its excavation began?
n633a8d20ae5.x: Lothal's excavation began in 1954; 1931 is the year for Chanhudaro. Harappa (1921) and Mohenjodaro (1922) are correct.

new.s: Stone-circle megalithic graves in Andhra are popularly called:
new.x: Stone-circle graves are called Rakshasa Gullu (also Pandava Gullu). Ash mounds are Neolithic and sarcophagi are terracotta coffins.

new.s: The largest collection of anthropomorphic megalithic figures in India is found in:
new.x: Tirupati has the largest collection of anthropomorphic (human-shaped) megalithic stones in India.

new.s: Sarcophagus (terracotta coffin) burials of Andhra are concentrated in:
new.x: Sarcophagi are concentrated in Chittoor and Anantapuramu; dolmens are found in Krishna, Chittoor and East Godavari.

new.s: Which megalithic burial type is NOT correctly matched with its form?
new.x: A menhir is an upright stone; the terracotta coffin is the sarcophagus.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about megalithic burials in Andhra:
1. Menhirs are concentrated in Krishna district.
2. Cist burials are numerous in Visakhapatnam.
3. Dolmens are found in Krishna and Chittoor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Menhirs (Krishna) and dolmens (Krishna, Chittoor, East Godavari) are rightly placed; 'many cist burials in Visakhapatnam' is keyed incorrect (G2 2025).

new.s: The typical pottery of the Megalithic (Iron Age) phase in Andhra is:
new.x: Black-and-red ware is the typical Megalithic pottery; painted pottery marks the Chalcolithic (Patapadu).

new.s: Ketavaram, known for prehistoric rock paintings, is in which district?
new.x: Ketavaram rock paintings are in Kurnool district; the Borra Caves are in Visakhapatnam.

new.s: The Borra Caves, a prehistoric cave site of Andhra, are in which district?
new.x: The Borra Caves are in Visakhapatnam; Ketavaram and the Kurnool caves are in Kurnool.

new.s: The animal most often painted in the prehistoric rock art of Andhra is the:
new.x: The deer is the most often painted animal in the rock art of the region.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about prehistoric rock art in Andhra:
1. Petroglyphs are carved, not painted.
2. Ketavaram rock paintings are in Visakhapatnam district.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Petroglyphs are carved images; Ketavaram is in Kurnool, not Visakhapatnam.

new.s: Utnur, a Neolithic ash-mound site, is located in:
new.x: Utnur, the Neolithic ash mound, is in Mahbubnagar district of Telangana.

new.s: The Neolithic settlements of Sanganakallu and Tekkalakota are in:
new.x: Sanganakallu and Tekkalakota are in Bellary district, Karnataka; Brahmagiri is in Chitradurga.

new.s: Palavoy, a Neolithic settlement, is in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
new.x: Palavoy is a Neolithic settlement in Anantapur district.

new.s: Which site on the right bank of the Krishna in Kurnool shows a Neolithic–Chalcolithic to Early Historic sequence?
new.x: Veerapuram in Kurnool, on the right bank of the Krishna, has a Neolithic–Chalcolithic to Early Historic sequence.

new.s: Keesarapalli in Krishna district is a Chalcolithic site known for:
new.x: Keesarapalli is known for copper tools; painted pottery is the feature of Patapadu.

new.s: Flakes, scrapers, borers and points are characteristic tools of the:
new.x: The Middle Palaeolithic is the flake stage; microliths belong to the Mesolithic.

new.s: Mesolithic weapons in Andhra were made of:
new.x: Mesolithic microliths were of chert and jasper, and weapons of dolomite; quartzite and limestone were Lower Palaeolithic materials.

new.s: Renigunta in Chittoor district is known for which Upper Palaeolithic industry?
new.x: Renigunta has an Upper Palaeolithic blade-and-burin industry.

new.s: Belum Caves in Kurnool are the ____ cave system in India.
new.x: Belum Caves in Kurnool form the second-longest cave system in India.

new.s: Giddaluru, Dornala and Yerragondapalem, Lower Palaeolithic sites, are in which district?
new.x: Giddaluru, Dornala, Yerragondapalem and Nandikanuma are Lower Palaeolithic sites of Prakasam district.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT listed among the microlithic centres of Andhra?
new.x: Utnur is a Neolithic ash-mound site; Giddaluru, Nagarjunakonda, Kondapur and Khammam are microlithic centres.

new.s: The microliths of Andhra resemble those of:
o: South India and the Caspian region
new.x: Andhra microliths resemble South Indian and Caspian microliths.

new.s: At Mehrgarh, pottery and cotton first appear in:
new.x: Period I was aceramic; pottery and cotton begin in Period II.

new.s: Copper working and wheel-made painted pottery at Mehrgarh begin in:
new.x: Copper working, wheel-made painted pottery and beads appear from Period III onward.

new.s: Burials at Mehrgarh were sometimes accompanied by which animals?
new.x: Mehrgarh burials, under or near houses and often flexed, sometimes included goats with ornaments and tools.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Mehrgarh:
1. Period I was aceramic and had mud-brick houses.
2. The dead were usually buried far from the houses.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Period I was aceramic with mud-brick houses; burials were under or near houses.

new.s: The Hakra culture of the Early Harappan phase is located in:
new.x: Hakra lies in the Ghaggar-Hakra area of Cholistan, not Gujarat.

new.s: The Sothi-Siswal culture of the Early Harappan phase belongs to which area?
new.x: Sothi-Siswal is the Early Harappan culture of the Rajasthan–Haryana area.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Early Harappan pottery?
o: Amri and Kot Diji wares were regional traditions
Early Harappans used the potter's wheel
Sothi-Siswal and Hakra wares were regional traditions
Early Harappan pottery was uniform across regions
new.x: Uniform pottery came only in the Mature phase; Early Harappan pottery had regional traditions.

new.s: Rana Ghundai, a farming and pastoral village, lies in which valley?
new.x: Rana Ghundai is in the Zhob-Loralai valley; Kili Gul Muhammad and Damb Sadaat are in the Quetta valley.

new.s: Amri was excavated in 1929 by:
new.x: N. G. Majumdar excavated Amri in 1929; it was later dug by J.-M. Casal.

new.s: Rana Ghundai was excavated by:
new.x: Rana Ghundai was excavated by E. J. Ross; Fairservis excavated Kili Gul Muhammad and Damb Sadaat.

new.s: Mitathal was excavated in 1968 by:
new.x: Suraj Bhan excavated Mitathal in 1968; R. S. Bisht excavated Banawali in 1974.

new.s: Kot Diji was excavated in 1955 by:
new.x: F. A. Khan excavated Kot Diji in 1955; Ghurye is also associated with the site.

new.s: Who held that the Harappan Civilisation arose by diffusion of ideas from West Asia?
new.x: Wheeler proposed West Asian diffusion; Mackay proposed migration from Sumer and Marshall indigenous evolution.

new.s: The criss-cross furrows of the ploughed field at Kalibangan-I indicate:
new.x: The criss-cross furrows of the earliest ploughed field show mixed cropping.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Kalibangan-I:
1. It has the earliest ploughed field.
2. Its fire altars belong to the pre-Harappan level.
3. It had a mud-brick fortification.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The ploughed field and mud-brick fortification belong to Kalibangan-I; fire altars belong to the Mature phase.

new.s: The crops of the Neolithic phase of Baluchistan and the Indus plains included:
new.x: Neolithic Baluchistan and the Indus plains grew wheat, barley, dates and cotton, with sheep and goats as main animals.

new.s: Which problem of Harappan origins remains unsolved?
o: The gap between Neolithic Mehrgarh and the urban phase
The use of the potter's wheel
new.x: The gap between Neolithic Mehrgarh and the urban phase remains unsolved.

new.s: In Mesopotamian records, Dilmun refers to:
new.x: Dilmun was the middle stop, Bahrain; Magan was Oman/Makran and Meluha the Indus region.

new.s: Which Harappan site is known as 'Mini Harappa'?
new.x: Lothal is called Mini Harappa; Mohenjodaro is the 'Mound of the Dead'.

new.s: Which Harappan site is called the 'Lancashire of India'?
new.x: Chanhudaro is called the Lancashire of India for its cotton.

new.s: Kotada is the local name of which Harappan site?
new.x: Dholavira is locally known as Kotada.

new.s: The term 'Indus Valley Civilisation' was coined by:
new.x: John Marshall coined 'Indus Valley Civilisation', now thought too narrow.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Kalibangan means 'black bangles'. Mohenjodaro is the Mound of the Dead, Lothal Mini Harappa and Magan Oman/Makran.

new.s: Dholavira, inscribed by UNESCO in 2021, is India's ____ World Heritage Site.
new.x: Dholavira became India's 40th and Gujarat's 4th World Heritage Site in 2021.

new.s: As of June 2026, Rakhigarhi's UNESCO status is:
new.x: Rakhigarhi is only on the Tentative List; Dholavira was inscribed in 2021 and Mohenjodaro in 1980.

new.s: In June 2026, the ASI transferred Rakhigarhi's 56 skeletons to the:
new.x: Under an MoU, the ASI transferred the 56 Mound 7 skeletons to the Anthropological Survey of India.

new.s: The second-largest Harappan site in India is:
new.x: Dholavira is the second-largest site in India after Rakhigarhi, and the fifth-largest IVC city.

new.s: The Late Harappan phase is dated to:
new.x: The Late Harappan phase (1900–1300 BCE) saw de-urbanisation; 2600–1900 BCE is the Mature phase.

new.s: John Marshall dated the Indus Civilisation to 3250–2750 BCE on the basis of:
new.x: Marshall used Mesopotamian cross-dating; D. P. Agrawal's radiocarbon dates gave about 2500–1750 BCE.

new.s: Sohgaura, often given as a decoy among Harappan sites, is a:
new.x: Sohgaura (Gorakhpur, on the Rapti) is a Mauryan copper-plate site, not Harappan; Burzahom has the pit dwellings.

new.s: The earliest evidence of garlic in the Harappan context comes from:
new.x: Balu has the earliest garlic; Kot Bala has the earliest furnace.

new.s: A dog buried with humans has been found at which Harappan site?
new.x: Ropar yielded a dog buried with humans, a steatite seal and oval pit burials.

new.s: Sinauli, with 125 graves, is in which district of Uttar Pradesh?
new.x: Sinauli (Baraut) is in Baghpat; Alamgirpur is in Meerut, Hulas in Saharanpur, Mandi in Muzaffarnagar.

new.s: Dholavira, found by J. P. Joshi, was excavated from 1990 by:
new.x: R. S. Bisht excavated Dholavira from 1990; J. P. Joshi had found it in 1967–68.

new.s: Rakhigarhi was excavated in 1997 by:
new.x: Amarendra Nath excavated Rakhigarhi in 1997.
